result.summary: Introduces `ChainstateManager::Now()` and a C/C++ API `btck_chainstate_manager_set_clock_time` / `SetClockTime` to allow kernel consumers and tests to set and query clock time on a per-chainstate-manager instance. Time-sensitive validation operations—including header future-time validation, IBD status evaluation (`IsTipRecent`), header pre-sync logging, and verification progress—are updated to read time through `ChainstateManager`. The PR also standardizes mempool time on `NodeClock::time_point` (`MempoolTime`) and segregates `NodeClock::now()` into a separate translation unit omitted from `libbitcoinkernel` to catch accidental nondeterministic clock usage at link time.
result.problem: Validation logic in `libbitcoinkernel` directly queried system time via process-global clock functions, preventing kernel library callers and tests from driving validation deterministically across multiple instances. Furthermore, uncoordinated queries to `NodeClock::now()` caused race conditions across second boundaries in tests like `chainstatemanager_ibd_exit_after_loading_blocks`.
evidence: Commit 79c304eacd explains an intermittent test failure: "The test set up the tip time using Now<NodeSeconds>() and then called UpdateIBDStatus(), which calls IsTipRecent(), which also calls Now<NodeSeconds>(). If a second boundary was crossed between the two calls, the tip_recent=true case would fail spuriously."
The PR description notes this provides an instance-scoped alternative to #35496 (which added global `btck_set_mock_time`), eliminating global state sharing between concurrent kernel instances.
result.scope_notes: The diff includes refactoring mempool time types from integers to `NodeClock::time_point` and adjusting link targets to disallow `NodeClock::now()` in `libbitcoinkernel`, which spans beyond `ChainstateManager` itself.
result.changed_since_previous: Adapted the `utxo_total_supply` fuzz harness and `chainstatemanager_ibd_exit_after_loading_blocks` unit test to directly exercise the per-chainman clock instead of relying on global mock clocks.
result.card: This pull request adds an instance-scoped clock override API (`btck_chainstate_manager_set_clock_time`) and routes validation time checks through `ChainstateManager::Now()`. This eliminates the kernel's reliance on host system clocks and process-global mock time, enabling independent, deterministic multi-instance validation while fixing an intermittent unit test race across second boundaries. It also converts mempool time representations to type-safe time points and enforces clock determinism by preventing `libbitcoinkernel` from linking against `NodeClock::now()`. No dependencies are required.

risk.why: A flaw in clock routing or time casting could alter block header future-time consensus checks or disrupt IBD latch transitions, potentially causing valid blocks to be rejected or nodes to stay in IBD indefinitely.
